subject: DeliverFlow performance & sizing workshop follow-up
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Wong <rachel.wong@deliverflow.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: DeliverFlow performance & sizing workshop follow-up

Hi Rachel — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can prepare a productive sizing workshop next week.

Call recap (short):
- Goal: validate latency SLOs and agree on throughput/capacity plan for the pilot (English support chat, conversational agent).
- Primary constraints you called out: p95 latency target for single-turn generation, streaming per-user concurrency for live agent assist, and short burst windows during marketing campaigns.

What we captured today (please correct if I misunderstood):
- Latency targets:
  - Target: p95 <= 200 ms for responses up to ~512 tokens (single-turn generation).
  - Acceptable tail: p99 <= 500 ms for 95% of traffic, degrade to smaller model variants if missed.
- Throughput / concurrency:
  - Steady-state: ~150 QPS (user-facing requests)
  - Peak bursts: up to ~900 QPS for 2–4 minute windows during promos
  - Streaming: typical concurrent streaming sessions ~180 (avg), worst-case concurrent streaming sessions ~1,200 (global) — per-user concurrency up to 20 streams during internal load tests
- Token characteristics:
  - Avg generated tokens per call: 120–220 tokens
  - Avg prompt + response tokens: 300–350 tokens
  - Expected token emission rate during streaming: up to ~9k tokens/sec across cluster during peak bursts

Immediate asks so our sizing workshop can be data-driven: 
1) Traffic sample: Please send a 72-hour synthetic/real traffic snippet with timestamped events (request timestamp, prompt token count, response token count, streaming start/stop markers) — we attached a CSV template to make this quick.
2) Confirm SLOs: If p95 is actually 250 ms instead of 200 ms, flag it in your reply so we size accordingly.
3) Failure mode: Share your desired failover behavior (queueing vs. graceful degrade to smaller model).
4) Identity & security: Does your SRE expect IP allow-lists or SSO + SAML for the Private pilot?

Tentative next steps / timeline:
- You: drop 72-hour sample + any retention / auditing constraints by Wed EOD (2026-06-16).
- Us (Sergio + infra): prepare initial capacity sketch and a 60–90 minute sizing workshop (we propose Thu 06/17 or Fri 06/18).
- Outcome: recommended capacity mix (dedicated GPUs + burst reserve), expected per-token unit cost range, and checklist for pilot cutover.

Attachments: deliverflow_workload_template.csv (fields: timestamp, req_id, user_id, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, streaming_flag, region)

If anything above is off, tell me — otherwise we’ll draft a preliminary sizing plan ahead of the workshop.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Rachel Wong <rachel.wong@deliverflow.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: DeliverFlow SRE <sre@deliverflow.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DeliverFlow performance & sizing workshop follow-up

Thanks Ben — great summary. Couple clarifications before we pull the sample together.

- We actually set our internal target to p95 <= 250 ms for the pilot (we can accept 200 ms as a stretch). Can you size to p95=250 ms by default and show sensitivity to 200 ms?
- The peak bursts profile was spot on but to be precise: our marketing bursts historically last 1–3 mins (rarely 4). Peak QPS is ~850 observed, with headroom target 1.1x (so ~935) — we'll include both observed and target headroom in the sample.
- Streaming: the per-user concurrency of 20 is measured during stress tests; production observed concurrent streams average 12 per user during warm hours.

We’ll attach a 72-hour sample and an anonymized SRE runbook. Delivering both by Wed EOD as requested.

Attached: deliverflow_72h_snippet.csv

Thanks,
Rachel Wong
Head of Platform Engineering | DeliverFlow
rachel.wong@deliverflow.com
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 06:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DeliverFlow performance & sizing workshop follow-up

I pulled the attached 72h sample and did a quick pass (see notes below). Ben — moving this to action for the workshop, and Laura FYI on sizing assumptions.

Quick observations from snippet (high level):
- 72h sample shows average QPS ~160, median request tokens ~95, median response tokens ~140. Peaks line up with marketing bursts — peak 1-min sustained at 820 QPS observed, top 30s crest hits ~1,050.
- Streaming markers: many sessions have long-lived connections with intermittent token emission; effective cluster token-rate spikes are very bursty (crest-to-basal ~6–8x).

Questions we need DeliverFlow to confirm before the workshop:
1) What is the acceptable stall behavior for streaming on transient model slowdowns? (buffer + resume vs. immediate client fallback)
2) For steady-state sizing, are you assuming provisioned concurrency per user or pooled concurrency? (impacts slot allocation)
3) Average response token distribution: is 140 tokens an upper median or do you expect a heavy tail into 400+ tokens for some flows?

Initial sizing sketch (very rough, subject to workshop validation):
- Basal load (steady 150–180 QPS, avg tokens ~240 total/request): 2–3 x 80GB GPUs with 8-bit quantized weights (for cost efficiency) should keep p95 under 250ms for non-streaming single-turns.
- Crest capacity (handling 1-minute 1k QPS spikes with streaming): add burst pool of 4 x 80GB GPU equivalents and autoscale triggers tied to request backlog + token emission rate.
- Streaming considerations: streaming sessions increase memory pressure due to KV cache — we should model average concurrent KV entries per active stream.

I attached a starter sizing workbook (redwood_initial_sizing_notes.xlsx) with the math — Ben, pls schedule workshop and share access to DeliverFlow's traffic and retention constraints so I can iterate.

Sergio
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai

Great — thanks Rachel and Sergio. Rachel: got the sample and runbook. We’ll use p95=250ms as the default scenario and include a sensitivity case for 200ms.

Next steps:
- Scheduling: I sent a Calendly link for a 60–75m workshop (please pick a slot Thu 06/17 or Fri 06/18).
- Prep: Sergio will circulate a short pre-read (deck + the sizing workbook) this afternoon.
- Deliverables: post-workshop we’ll provide a recommended capacity mix, expected per-token cost band, and a pilot cutover checklist (including SSO/allow-list notes).

If anyone needs a sandbox access earlier, let me know and I’ll request a short-term dev key for DeliverFlow SRE.

Thanks,
Ben
